title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and foot discomfort.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports persistent tingling and numbness in both feet, which he describes as a sensation of "walking on cotton." He states these symptoms have been constant for several months. He has been on long-term insulin therapy and denies any recent episodes of severe low blood sugar. He reports adherence to his current treatment regimen.

Medication List
Long-acting insulin.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination of the lower extremities reveals diminished sensation to light touch and monofilament testing in the distal toes bilaterally. No active ulcers or skin breakdown noted on the feet.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
2. Polyneuropathy.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. We will monitor blood glucose levels and discuss further management of the peripheral neuropathy symptoms. The patient was instructed to inspect his feet daily for any signs of injury. Follow up in three months.
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: the combination code E11.42 captures both.
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Coding the two separately misses the presumed link.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
